skill.name: mcp-resources-guide
skill.description: Guide Rust MCP server authors in implementing resources with URI schemes, listing, fetching, MIME handling, caching, streaming, and tests.
skill.summary: Build MCP resources for files, records, API data, caching, streaming, and resource tests.
skill.author: EmilLindfors

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by markdown code fences or illustrative Rust examples, not active command execution, secret access, or obfuscation. The audit found real insecure guidance in the examples: file URI parsing can escape a configured root, symlink following can expose unintended files, and a database example builds SQL from URI-derived table text.

remediation.issue: File resource examples can read paths outside the intended root.
remediation.suggestion: Canonicalize the requested path and root, reject absolute paths and parent traversal, and require the canonical target to remain under the allowed root before reading text or binary files.

remediation.issue: Database resource example interpolates a URI-derived table name into SQL.
remediation.suggestion: Replace dynamic table names with a fixed allowlist or enum mapping, and keep untrusted values in bound parameters only.

remediation.issue: Documentation listing follows symlinks without showing boundary checks.
remediation.suggestion: Disable symlink following by default, or verify each canonical target remains inside the documentation directory before listing it.

semantic_findings.title: Path Traversal Risk in File Resource Examples
semantic_findings.description: The file resource examples strip the file URI prefix and join the remaining path to a root directory without canonicalization, allowlisting, or rejection of absolute and parent-directory paths. Copied code could expose files outside the intended resource root.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example directly converts the URI suffix into a PathBuf and reads root_path.join(path). Rust path joining can escape the root when the child is absolute, and parent traversal is not blocked.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe Dynamic SQL From Resource URI
semantic_findings.description: The database resource example reads the table name from the db URI and inserts it into a SELECT statement with string formatting. The record id is bound, but the table identifier is not allowlisted or quoted safely.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The table variable comes from URI parts and is interpolated into SQL text. This is a clear unsafe pattern if the example is copied into a real MCP server.

semantic_findings.title: Symlink Traversal During Resource Listing
semantic_findings.description: The documentation resource example enables symlink following while walking a documentation directory. Without canonical path checks, linked files outside the intended directory could be listed as resources.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example explicitly calls follow_links(true) during directory walking. The surrounding code strips the documentation root but does not show checks that canonical targets remain inside it.

content.value_statement: MCP server authors need repeatable patterns for exposing files, records, and API data as resources. This skill guides URI design, listing, fetching, MIME handling, caching, streaming, and testing for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Explains URI schemes and templates for file, database, API, and metrics resources.
Shows Rust rmcp examples for listing resources and fetching resource content.
Covers MIME type selection for text, markdown, JSON, Rust, TOML, and binary data.
Describes in-memory caching, lazy loading, and TTL-based cache checks.
Outlines tests for valid URIs, invalid URIs, edge cases, and performance.
limitations: Examples are instructional and need security hardening before production use.
It does not provide a complete runnable MCP server scaffold.
It does not cover authentication, authorization, or tenant isolation in detail.
It focuses on Rust rmcp patterns rather than other MCP SDKs.

use_cases.title: Expose Project Files as Resources
use_cases.description: Design URI schemes, metadata, MIME types, and fetch behavior for project documentation or source files.

use_cases.title: Model Database Records as Resources
use_cases.description: Plan how database records should be addressed, listed, fetched, cached, and represented for assistant context.

use_cases.title: Optimize Large Resource Delivery
use_cases.description: Apply caching, lazy loading, binary handling, and streaming patterns for large or expensive resource sources.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Basic Resource
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design an MCP resource for [data source]. Include the URI scheme, listed metadata, MIME type, and expected fetch result.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Resource Templates
prompt_templates.prompt: Create resource URI templates for [entities]. Explain list behavior, fetch behavior, invalid URI handling, and example resource names.

prompt_templates.title: Review Resource Security
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my MCP resource design for path traversal, SQL injection, credential exposure, authorization gaps, cache leakage, and unsafe URI parsing.

prompt_templates.title: Design Caching and Streaming
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a caching, invalidation, and streaming strategy for MCP resources backed by [large or expensive source]. Include limits, errors, and tests.

output_examples.input: Design resources for a documentation folder.
output: Use a docs resource scheme with paths relative to the documentation root.
List markdown files with names, descriptions, and text/markdown MIME types.
Validate paths before fetching and keep fetched content inside the allowed root.
Cache metadata separately from document content when files change often.

output_examples.output: The review identifies table allowlisting, record-level authorization, parameter binding, cache TTLs, and tests for invalid URIs.

output: Use size limits before reading binary content.
Return accurate MIME types and avoid converting binary data to text.
Stream or paginate large content instead of buffering everything in memory.

best_practices: Validate every URI component before using it in filesystem paths, database queries, or API URLs.
Document resource schemes, MIME types, cache lifetimes, and invalidation rules.
Keep resource fetching read-only, observable, and covered by success and failure tests.
anti_patterns: Joining URI paths directly to filesystem roots without canonicalization.
Building SQL identifiers or queries from URI text without an allowlist.
Caching sensitive or tenant-specific resources without scoped keys and expiry.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps you design MCP resources that expose files, database records, API responses, metrics, and binary data to AI assistants.

faq.question: Which programming stack does it target?
faq.answer: It targets Rust MCP servers that use the rmcp crate, although the resource design ideas are broadly useful.

faq.question: Does it generate a complete server?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns, examples, review prompts, and implementation guidance rather than a full application scaffold.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is written for MCP resource design and can support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does it cover security?
faq.answer: It mentions validation and traversal prevention, but some examples need stronger production security controls.

faq.question: When should I use MCP resources instead of tools?
faq.answer: Use resources for read-only context such as files or records. Use tools for actions, mutations, and computations.
